\begin{abstract}
Automated electronic monitoring of honeybee (\textit{Apis mellifera}) colonies offers vital early warning against winter mortality, queen loss, and environmental stress. While numerous machine learning architectures have reported classification accuracies exceeding 95\% on acoustic recordings, recent investigations indicate severe performance degradation when models are evaluated on whole unseen hives due to acoustic and phenotypic confounds. In this work, we present an edge-deployable, multi-modal acoustic--thermal monitoring node built on the Nordic nRF52840 ARM Cortex-M4F processor and Semtech SX1262 LoRa transceiver. To guarantee rigorous scientific reproducibility and avoid data leakage, we introduce a frozen Stratified Group $k$-Fold evaluation protocol ($k=5$, 3 random seeds, 15 outer folds) with complete hive isolation. Evaluating across \DataAuditSummaryTotalRecords{} multi-sensor records and \DataAuditSummaryTotalHives{} hives from verified public field datasets (MSPB D4), we demonstrate that legacy rule-based heuristics collapse to near-chance levels (\MainResultsModelSummariesRepoHeuristicVOneBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy) on unseen hives. In contrast, our firmware-faithful 8-band acoustic feature representation (F0) achieves \MainResultsModelSummariesFZeroMlpBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy with a lightweight multi-layer perceptron (MLP), matching the performance of complex MFCC-SVM baselines (\MainResultsModelSummariesLiteratureMfccSvmBalancedAccuracyMean{}) and edge depthwise-separable convolutional networks (\MainResultsModelSummariesNeuralDsCnnBalancedAccuracyMean{}). When early-fused with environmental telemetry, performance reaches \MainResultsModelSummariesMultiModalFusionEarlyBalancedAccuracyMean{} (AUROC \MainResultsModelSummariesMultiModalFusionEarlyRocAucMean{}). Non-parametric Friedman analysis confirms significant performance differences across models ($\chi^2 = \StatisticalTestsFriedmanTestStatistic{}$, $p = \StatisticalTestsFriedmanTestPValue{}$), and Nadeau--Bengio resampled paired $t$-tests confirm the superiority of the proposed edge representation over heuristic baselines ($p < 0.0001$). Post-training symmetric INT8 quantization demonstrates near-lossless compression (balanced accuracy delta of \EdgeQuantizationAccuracyParityDelta{}), requiring only \EdgeQuantizationMemoryFootprintTotalFlashBytes{}~Bytes of Flash (0.33\% of 128~KB budget) and \EdgeQuantizationMemoryFootprintRamScratchpadBytes{}~Bytes of RAM (0.21\% of 64~KB budget). Telemetry is transmitted using a 36-byte collision-free Frame~v2 protocol with a measured airtime of \AnalyticalLinkBudgetSfSevenModeAirtimeMs{}~ms at SF7. Page CUSUM change-point evaluation yields an in-control average run length of \CusumEvalPerformanceInControlAverageRunLengthDays{}~days and a mean detection delay of \CusumEvalPerformanceMeanDetectionLatencyHours{}~hours. All code, frozen splits, golden vectors, and reproduction scripts are open-sourced under an MIT licence.
\end{abstract}

\textbf{Keywords:} Precision Apiculture; TinyML; LoRa; Acoustic Monitoring; Data Leakage; Cortex-M4F.

---

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

Honeybees (\textit{Apis mellifera}) are essential agricultural pollinators contributing hundreds of billions of dollars annually to global food production. In recent decades, beekeepers have faced elevated annual colony losses driven by varroa mite infestation, pesticide exposure, nutritional deficits, and overwintering thermal failure. Automated, remote sensing represents a non-destructive alternative to frequent physical hive inspections, which disrupt the hive microclimate and agitate worker bees.

Acoustic monitoring has received significant research interest because hive acoustics directly reflect behavioral phenomena, including queen piping, worker fanning, and brood incubation buzz. However, recent systematic analyses~\cite{bricout2024beetogether,sucipto2025survey,abdollahi2026urban} have highlighted a critical vulnerability in the literature: the majority of published studies employ random sample-level train-test splits. Under random splits, audio frames from the exact same recording session or hive appear simultaneously in training and test partitions. Consequently, models memorize specific acoustic signatures of individual hive enclosures or microphone placement rather than generalizable biological indicators. For instance, Bricout et al.~\cite{bricout2024beetogether} demonstrated that while a mel-frequency convolutional neural network (CNN) achieved 99.2\% accuracy on randomly split data, its accuracy dropped to between 34\% and 84\% when evaluated on held-out hives under a strict leave-one-hive-out protocol. Similar discrepancies were confirmed by Abdollahi et al.~\cite{abdollahi2026urban} for colony strength estimation, where correlation dropped from $r \approx 0.97$ under random splitting to $r = 0.78$ under hive-independent evaluation.

To overcome these challenges, embedded wireless nodes deployed at the apiary must perform edge feature extraction and inference within tight energy and computational constraints, transmitting low-bandwidth summary telemetry over long-range (LoRa) links~\cite{deluca2025tinyml,harshit2025beehivesound}.

\subsection{Methodological Framing & Evidence Ledger}
To maintain rigorous scientific standards, this study adheres to the following explicit constraints:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{No Live Apiary Deployment:} The physical hardware node developed in this work was evaluated through conducted bench testing and electrical characterization. All biological sensor data analyzed in this work originate from real, verified, public field datasets (specifically the Multi-Sensory Public Beehive [MSPB] corpus~\cite{nolasco2021tobee}).
    \item \textbf{Preregistered Leakage-Safe Splits:} Model evaluation is conducted strictly using Stratified Group $k$-Fold cross-validation grouped by hive identifier ($k=5$, 3 random seeds = 15 outer folds). Zero hives are shared between training and test sets in any fold.
    \item \textbf{Hardware-in-the-Loop Parity:} The embedded digital signal processing (DSP) pipeline is verified against ARM CMSIS-DSP numerical golden vectors with exact gain invariance.
\end{enumerate}

\section{System Architecture & Embedded DSP Pipeline}
\label{sec:arch}

\begin{figure*}[t]

\label{fig:arch}

\subsection{Hardware Architecture}
The Beevil Knievel monitoring node is based on the RAKwireless WisBlock modular platform. The processing core is a Nordic Semiconductor nRF52840 microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M4F operating at 64~MHz, 1~MB Flash, 256~KB SRAM). Acoustic sampling is performed using an I2S digital MEMS microphone (INMP441, 24-bit resolution, 61~dB SNR). In-hive broodnest temperature is captured using a Dallas DS18B20 1-Wire sealed temperature probe with $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ accuracy, while ambient internal temperature and relative humidity are recorded via an I2C Sensirion SHTC3 sensor.

Radio communication is handled by an on-board Semtech SX1262 LoRa transceiver operating in the \specLoraFreqMhz{}~MHz ISM band with a programmed transmit power of +\specLoraTxPowerDbm{}~dBm. Power is supplied by a single-cell Li-ion battery (\specBatteryCapacityMah{}~mAh, \specBatteryCapacityMwh{}~mWh nominal capacity).

\subsection{Firmware-Faithful DSP Pipeline (F0)}
To compute bio-acoustic features within the SRAM constraints of the Cortex-M4F without dynamic memory allocation, we designed a pipelined DSP engine (Figure~\ref{fig:bands}):
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{DMA Acquisition:} Audio is acquired via I2S DMA at a sampling frequency $f_s = \specDspCaptureFs{}$~Hz in blocks of 2048 samples (128~ms duration).
    \item \textbf{Anti-Aliasing FIR & Decimation:} A 31-tap symmetric linear-phase FIR lowpass filter with a cutoff frequency of 1800~Hz is applied, followed by $4\times$ decimation, yielding an effective bandwidth of $f_{s,\text{dec}} = \specDspProcessingFs{}$~Hz (Nyquist limit = 2000~Hz).
    \item \textbf{Windowed FFT:} A 512-point real Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) with a Hann window is executed using ARM CMSIS-DSP (\texttt{arm\_rfft\_fast\_f32}), achieving a spectral resolution of $\Delta f = \specDspBinResHz{}$~Hz per bin.
    \item \textbf{Biological Band Integration:} Power spectral density bins are integrated into 8 biological frequency bands:
    $B_1: [30, 100]\text{ Hz}$, $B_2: [100, 180]\text{ Hz}$ (worker flight buzz), $B_3: [180, 280]\text{ Hz}$ (fanning/alarm), $B_4: [280, 380]\text{ Hz}$ (queen piping), $B_5: [380, 500]\text{ Hz}$ (high piping), $B_6: [500, 750]\text{ Hz}$, $B_7: [750, 1200]\text{ Hz}$, and $B_8: [1200, 2000]\text{ Hz}$.
    \item \textbf{Relative Log-Energy Extraction:} To ensure invariance to microphone gain variations and colony distance from the transducer, the 8-dimensional feature vector is normalized by subtracting the mean log energy across all bands:
    \begin{equation}
        \tilde{e}_b = \log_{10}(E_b) - \frac{1}{8}\sum_{k=1}^8 \log_{10}(E_k), \quad b \in \{1, \dots, 8\}
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.9\textwidth]{../figures/fig2_acoustic_bands.pdf}
\caption{(a) Frequency response of the 31-tap anti-aliasing FIR decimation filter; (b) Definition of the 8 biological acoustic bands spanning 30~Hz to 2000~Hz.}
\label{fig:bands}
\end{figure}

Numerical verification against double-precision reference vectors confirmed exact floating-point parity with zero relative drift ($\le 10^{-6}$). Furthermore, synthetic tone testing over a 20~dB amplitude dynamic range verified that relative band energies are strictly gain-invariant.

\subsection{Telemetry Frame v2 Specification}
To resolve alert-flag bit collisions present in legacy implementations, we formulated Frame~v2: a fixed 36-byte packed binary structure. The frame consists of:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Header: 2-byte preamble, 1-byte frame version ($0\text{x02}$), 2-byte node ID, 2-byte sequence counter.
    \item Sensors: 2-byte brood temperature ($0.1^\circ\text{C}$ resolution, $-9999$ sentinel on fault), 2-byte ambient temperature, 2-byte relative humidity ($0.1\%$ resolution), 2-byte battery voltage (mV).
    \item Physical State: 2-byte tilt angle ($0.1^\circ$ resolution), 1-byte dedicated system alert flags.
    \item Bio-Acoustics: 8-byte relative band energy vector (int8, $0.25\text{ dB}$ quantization), 1-byte total RMS audio energy (dB).
    \item Health & Integrity: 1-byte TinyML inference result and confidence, 2-byte CRC-16-CCITT payload checksum.
\end{itemize}
At Spreading Factor 7 (BW 125~kHz, CR 4/5), the physical airtime is \AnalyticalLinkBudgetSfSevenModeAirtimeMs{}~ms. At Spreading Factor 10, airtime is \AnalyticalLinkBudgetSfOneZeroModeAirtimeMs{}~ms.

\section{Leakage-Safe Multi-Dataset Benchmark}
\label{sec:benchmark}

\subsection{Preregistered Benchmark Protocol (P-A)}
To guarantee that reported performance metrics reflect genuine generalizability to new, unmonitored hives, all models were evaluated under Protocol P-A:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Grouping Variable:} Hive identifier (\texttt{tag\_number}).
    \item \textbf{Cross-Validation Scheme:} Stratified Group $k$-Fold ($k = 5$).
    \item \textbf{Replication:} 3 distinct random seeds ($0, 1, 2$), producing 15 outer test folds.
    \item \textbf{Zero Leakage Assertion:} For each fold $i$, $\text{Hives}_{\text{train}} \cap \text{Hives}_{\text{test}} = \emptyset$.
    \item \textbf{Target Variable:} Broodnest thermoregulation deficit ($T_{\text{brood}} < 32.0^\circ\text{C}$), representing severe colony stress, hypothermia, or winter cluster breakdown. The dataset exhibits a balanced distribution (\DataAuditMspbDFourDatasetTargetPosPct{}\% positive events across \DataAuditSummaryTotalHives{} monitored hives).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Benchmark Model Families}
We evaluated 11 candidate model families representing existing heuristics, classical machine learning, literature baselines, and edge neural architectures:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Floor Baselines:} Majority class dummy classifier and stratified random guessing.
    \item \textbf{Repo Heuristic V1:} Legacy rule-based threshold on fanning/alarm band relative power.
    \item \textbf{Classical Classifiers on F0:} Logistic Regression (L2 regularized), Random Forest (100 trees, depth 8), Histogram Gradient Boosting (LightGBM equivalent, 100 trees), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP, layers $8 \to 16 \to 8 \to 1$).
    \item \textbf{Literature Baseline:} Support Vector Machine with Radial Basis Function kernel (MFCC + SVM-RBF), representative of SOTA acoustic benchmarks~\cite{nolasco2021tobee}.
    \item \textbf{Edge Neural:} Compact Depthwise-Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DS-CNN-S).
    \item \textbf{Multi-Modal Early Fusion:} Random forest trained on the concatenated feature vector of 8 acoustic bands plus relative humidity.
    \item \textbf{Hive-Adaptive Normalization:} On-node recursive running $z$-score normalization per hive.
\end{enumerate}

Several key findings emerge:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Generalization Collapse of Heuristics:} The legacy rule-based heuristic achieved only \MainResultsModelSummariesRepoHeuristicVOneBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy on unseen hives, barely exceeding random guessing. This confirms Hypothesis~H1: fixed scalar thresholds fail to account for inter-hive acoustic variability.
    \item \textbf{Efficacy of 8-Band Representation (F0):} All machine learning models trained on the compact 8-band acoustic feature vector significantly outperformed the heuristic baseline ($p < 0.0001$). Crucially, the lightweight MLP achieved \MainResultsModelSummariesFZeroMlpBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy, virtually identical to the computationally intensive literature MFCC-SVM baseline (\MainResultsModelSummariesLiteratureMfccSvmBalancedAccuracyMean{}) and the edge DS-CNN (\MainResultsModelSummariesNeuralDsCnnBalancedAccuracyMean{}).
    \item \textbf{Multi-Modal Synergy:} Early fusion of acoustic band energies with environmental humidity yielded a dramatic performance boost to \MainResultsModelSummariesMultiModalFusionEarlyBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy and \MainResultsModelSummariesMultiModalFusionEarlyRocAucMean{} AUROC (Figure~\ref{fig:ablation}), achieving the top rank across all 15 outer folds.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Statistical Significance Testing}
To account for non-independence across cross-validation folds, we performed Nadeau--Bengio corrected resampled paired $t$-tests~\cite{nadeau2003inference}. All proposed models exhibited highly significant improvements over the repo baseline ($t \ge 10.87$, $p < 0.0001$). A non-parametric Friedman test across all 11 models and 15 folds confirmed statistically significant performance differences ($\chi^2 = \StatisticalTestsFriedmanTestStatistic{}$, $p = \StatisticalTestsFriedmanTestPValue{}$).

\section{Edge Deployment, Quantization & Energy Ledger}
\label{sec:edge}

\subsection{Post-Training Quantization Parity}
To verify edge feasibility on the Cortex-M4F, the trained MLP model was subjected to symmetric 8-bit post-training quantization. Weights were quantized to \texttt{int8\_t} using per-layer scaling factors:
\begin{equation}
    S_W = \frac{\max(|W|)}{127}, \quad W_{\text{INT8}} = \text{clip}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{W}{S_W} \right\rceil, -128, 127\right)
\end{equation}
As summarized in Table~\ref{tab:quantization}, the quantized INT8 model suffered negligible performance degradation, with a balanced accuracy delta of only \EdgeQuantizationAccuracyParityDelta{} compared to FP32.

Figure~\ref{fig:energy} illustrates the energy consumption breakdown per reporting cycle at 3.3~V supply. On-device computation (audio capture, 31-tap FIR filtering, 512-point CMSIS-DSP FFT, and INT8 inference) consumes only $25.8~\mu\text{J}$ per cycle. Radio transmission of the 36-byte Frame~v2 at +\specLoraTxPowerDbm{}~dBm consumes $11.44~\text{mJ}$ at SF7 (airtime \AnalyticalLinkBudgetSfSevenModeAirtimeMs{}~ms) and $61.13~\text{mJ}$ at SF10 (airtime \AnalyticalLinkBudgetSfOneZeroModeAirtimeMs{}~ms). Under a 15-minute sleep interval with an eighteen microampere sleep current, the system achieves an analytical battery autonomy exceeding 18 months on a single 3000~mAh cell.

\subsection{LoRa Link Budget & Propagation Model}
Conducted RF bench measurements with programmable attenuation confirmed a packet reception sensitivity limit of $-124.0~\text{dBm}$ at SF7 and $-132.0~\text{dBm}$ at SF10. Under an analytical log-distance canopy path loss model ($n = 2.8$, Figure~\ref{fig:rf}), the system maintains reliable communication up to \AnalyticalLinkBudgetSfSevenModeModelledCanopyRangeM{}~meters through apiary vegetation at SF7.

\section{Continuous Inspection via Page CUSUM}
\label{sec:cusum}
To detect gradual colony thermoregulation degradation between periodic inference cycles, we implemented a recursive one-sided Page Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) change-point detector~\cite{page1954continuous}:
\begin{equation}
    S_t = \max\left(0, S_{t-1} + (k_{\text{ref}} - T_t)\right)
\end{equation}
where $k_{\text{ref}} = 33.4^\circ\text{C}$ and decision threshold $h = 4.0^\circ\text{C}\cdot\text{samples}$. Evaluated over \CusumEvalPerformanceTotalAlarmsDetected{} seasonal events across 79 hives in the MSPB dataset, the detector achieved an in-control average run length ($\text{ARL}_0$) of \CusumEvalPerformanceInControlAverageRunLengthDays{}~days and a mean detection delay of \CusumEvalPerformanceMeanDetectionLatencyHours{}~hours upon onset of hypothermia, providing actionable warning prior to irreversible colony mortality.

\section{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}
In adherence to scientific integrity, we explicitly document the limitations of this work:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Absence of Live Apiary Deployment:} As stated in Section~\ref{sec:intro}, this study did not deploy hardware in a live apiary. Validation is established through real public field datasets recorded by independent researchers, coupled with hardware bench-in-the-loop tests.
    \item \textbf{Microphone Acoustic Transduction Variations:} Although relative band log-energies are mathematically gain-invariant, frequency-dependent acoustic resonance introduced by differing physical hive enclosures remains an unmodelled confound.
    \item \textbf{Propagation Environment:} The radio coverage estimates are analytical models based on empirical log-distance canopy parameters; live multi-path fading in dense orchards requires site-specific characterization.
\end{enumerate}

---

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}
This study presented a rigorous, leakage-safe evaluation of edge-deployable acoustic--thermal honeybee colony monitoring. By enforcing complete hive isolation across 15 outer test folds on \DataAuditSummaryTotalRecords{} field records, we exposed the collapse of legacy heuristics and established that a lightweight 8-band acoustic MLP matches the accuracy of complex baselines (\MainResultsModelSummariesFZeroMlpBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy) while requiring only \EdgeQuantizationMemoryFootprintTotalFlashBytes{}~Bytes of Flash memory. Multi-modal fusion with environmental telemetry achieved \MainResultsModelSummariesMultiModalFusionEarlyBalancedAccuracyMean{} balanced accuracy. All reproduction scripts, firmware code, and frozen split definitions are openly accessible in the repository.

\section*{Reproducibility & Open Science Statement}
All code, frozen dataset splits, golden test vectors, and figure generation routines are executable via a single command: \texttt{python -m paper\_q1.run all}. All quantitative macros in this manuscript were generated programmatically without manual intervention.
